_comment: PathTriage Primitive 02 — IAM modification (assign) preventive SCP. Denies self-attach of admin-equivalent policies. Companion to the detection query in cloudtrail_lake_query.sql.

_notes.coverage: First statement denies self-attach of the three most common admin-equivalent AWS-managed policies. Second statement enforces a positive tag-based control: only principals tagged 'iam-mgmt-authorized=true' or matching approved role name patterns can perform IAM assign actions.
_notes.self_attach_limitation: The iam:UserName condition variable only matches for IAM users, not for assumed-role sessions. Self-attach via a role that assumes itself would bypass statement 1; the second statement (tag-based) covers this by requiring positive authorization for any IAM assignment.
_notes.inline_policy_gap: SCPs cannot match inline policy content, so a caller with iam:PutUserPolicy could still self-assign an inline policy with wildcard actions. Detection primitive catches this at runtime.
_notes.cross_role_delegation: An attacker with permission to assume role A could have A attach a policy to role B, bypassing the caller-target identity match in statement 1. Statement 2 (tag-based) blocks this if role A is not tag-authorized.
_notes.deployment: Attach at the organisation root. Requires all legitimate IAM-management identities to be tagged 'iam-mgmt-authorized=true' before deployment (audit before enabling to avoid locking out ops teams).
